text.tspan: A stochastic birth-death process (a) with subclones with
custom parameters (b), and reversible epi-genetic events (c).
The parameters of the birth-death process can vary in time to
simulate therapy (a) effect and model negative selection (b).
Modes of cell divison on the tissue
Tissue evolution is stochastic and depends on cell parameters.
Divisions happen uniformly on the lattice (a) or on boundaries (b).
A tissue is a squared lattice (a), with cells positioned in a discrete
coordinate system (b), and pushing each other during simulation.
Custom driver events per mutant (a) and passenger mutation
Single-cell phylogenies are generaeted from tissue samples (a),
capturing epi-mutations with different heritability patterns (b).
The tissue can be sampled at single (a) or multiple time-points,
Mutation occurrence counts data in VCF format, NovaSeq error
model (a), to create variant allele frequency data (b).
SAM output can be streamlined with standard bioinformatics
Germline reference from the UK biobank samples (a), with
possibility of simulating whole-genome sequencing datasets (b).
Time-varying mutational exposures to emulate enviroment
Somatic events are mapped on branches of the simulated
phylogeny according to active mutational signatures.
